citations.narrative:
The dealer has not maintained records which correctly disclose the following information regarding animals purchased
and sold by the dealer. Four bobcat records have incorrect acquisition dates documented and three of those four records
also have incorrect disposition dates documented. Additionally, one of those four bobcats and one additional bobcat have
incorrect birth dates documented on disposition paperwork supplied to a purchaser. Because of the incorrect recorded
acquisition, disposition, and birth dates, it was difficult to trace animal movement.
Correct record keeping is necessary to properly identify animals and to accurately trace animals to ensure their legal
acquisition, health, and humane transportation.
Every dealer shall make, keep, and maintain records or forms which fully and correctly disclose acquisition and
disposition information regarding animals purchased or otherwise acquired, owned, held, leased, or otherwise in his or her
possession or under his or her control, or which is transported, sold, euthanized, or otherwise disposed of by that dealer.
Correct by September 30, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
